pr_title: network: introduce BPF to reject netlink messages about non-static neighbor
pr_comments:
BTW, in libsystemd-network, all BPF op codes are merged with `+`. But, should not this be `|`?
In this PR, I follow the syntax in libsystemd-network, that is, using `+`.
WDYT?

neat stuff. love it.

as long as the bitmasks are orthogonal I guess `+` vs. `|` doesn't really matter. I'd probably do it the way everybody else does it ;-)

So the original BSD docs all use `+`, so I'd stick to that I guess:

https://www.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=bpf&sektion=4

issue_context.title: Excessive CPU use by systemd-networkd during arp storm in network
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
 > 245

**Used distribution**
 > Ubuntu 20.04

**Linux kernel version used** (`uname -a`)
 > `Linux foobar 5.4.0-88-generic #99-Ubuntu SMP Thu Sep 23 17:29:00 UTC 2021 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux`

**CPU architecture issue was seen on**
 > x86_64

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 > Low CPU usage

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
 > 100% CPU usage by systemd-networkd

**Steps to reproduce the problem**
 1. Create L2 loop between two (or more) vxlan interfaces with enabled arp on both vxlan interfaces.
 2. wait until BUM reaches ~ 50-100 Mbps
 3. Check CPU usage by systemd-networkd.

**Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue**
I found that systemd-networkd is listening on AF_NETLINK (which is fine) but recieves huge amount of RTM_NEWNEIGH messages. I'm not sure that systemd-networkd should be interested in updates in arp tables. If there are too much of updates, systemd-networkd unexpectedly start to become high-volume application.
